name: package.json
summary: Frontend project manifest defining package metadata, dependency graph, module type, and build lifecycle scripts
purpose: Central configuration file that enables the Node.js package manager ecosystem to install third-party libraries, execute standardized build/test/run commands, and maintain consistent project identity and behavior across development, CI/CD, and production environments.
responsibilities: Declare project identity and versioning (name, version, private)
Catalog runtime dependencies required by the frontend application
Catalog development dependencies such as build tools, linters, and test frameworks
Define executable scripts for development, building, testing, and deployment workflows
Signal the JavaScript module system (ES modules vs CommonJS) via the type field
Serve as the root contract for package managers to resolve and install the dependency tree
inputs: Dependency declarations with semantic version ranges
Shell commands mapped to script names
outputs: Resolved node_modules directory containing installed packages
Build artifacts generated by script execution
Dependency tree information consumed by bundlers and IDEs
architecture_notes: This manifest sits at the root of the frontend package and acts as the single source of truth for external dependencies and build orchestration. The separation between dependencies and devDependencies enforces the architectural boundary between runtime libraries (shipped to the browser) and build-time tooling (executed by Node.js on the server). The scripts field provides an abstraction layer over the build pipeline, decoupling developer workflows from specific tool implementations. The type field influences how downstream tools interpret source files, particularly relevant for modern bundlers adopting native ESM. As a frontend package, this file likely drives a module bundler whose configuration consumes these declarations.
improvements: Add an engines field to enforce minimum Node.js and package manager versions
Introduce a packageManager field for deterministic package manager selection
Add explicit workspace configuration if this is part of a monorepo
Include a browserslist configuration or dependency to define the target browser matrix
Add integrity verification fields or enforce lockfile usage in CI for reproducible installs
Document script purposes in a README or inline comments if supported by the package manager
